newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Anshan cuts 97 steel product export figures.
newsitem.headline: China Anshan cuts 97 steel product export figures.

text.p: The mammoth Anshan Iron and Steel complex in north China has cut its 1997 steel products export estimates, pending reviews of North American steel plate anti-dumping laws, an industry source said on Tuesday.

"Anshan's exports of steel products may not even reach 850,000 tonnes this year, compared to 880,000 tonnes exported in 1996 and 1.4 million tonnes exported in 1995," the source told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
"The U.S. and Canada are investigating the steel plate situation and if China does not come out favorably then we may not have easy access to those markets for steel plates," the source said.
Cheaper Russian and Ukrainian steel plates exported to North American had caused much of the problem, the source said.

Steel plates made up a large percentage of Anshan's steel products exports, with 300,000 tonnes of steel plates exported in 1996 out of the total 880,000 tonnes of steel products exported that year, the source said.
China's steel plates were priced at about $320 per tonne, FOB China, but Russian and Ukrainian material was much cheaper, the source said.
The industry source was participating in the week-long fair in Hong Kong sponsored by the China Iron and Steel Industry and Trade Group Corp (CSGC) and China Metallurgic (Hong Kong) Company Ltd.

The Canadian government said last month it was investigating the alleged dumping of hot-rolled carbon steel plate by a number of offshore producers like China, Russia, Mexico, Poland and South Africa.
The federal agency Revenue Canada expected to reach a decision by mid-May.

The U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) said last December it had found "reasonable indication" that American markets were being hurt by cheaper steel plate imports from China, Russia and Ukraine.
The ITC is due to release a final report on April 14, and the investigation could eventually lead to anti-dumping duties being imposed.

The iron and steel behemoth in Anshan city, which is known as the city of steel, is located in the northern Chinese province of Liaoning and produces about 8.5 million tonnes of iron per year and 8.6 million tonnes of steel per year, the source said.
Anshan makes about 6.6 million tonnes of steel products per year, the source said.
The complex employs about 400,000 people and contains schools and hospitals in addition to its six mines, one iron factory and three steel factories, the source said.
